q: 1. A pipe sunk into the ground to tap the underground water is called .............
explain: A tube well consists of a pipe (casing) driven into the ground to reach an aquifer, through which water is pumped.

q: 2. The earth's water circulatory system is known as .............
explain: The hydrological cycle describes the continuous movement of water on, above, and below the surface of the Earth.

q: 3. The yield of an underground source may be obtained by .............
explain: Pumping tests and recuperation tests are standard field procedures to determine the sustainable yield of a well.

q: 4. Colloidal impurities if associated with organic matter having bacteria becomes the chief sources of .............
explain: Organic colloidal matter provides a breeding ground for bacteria, leading to widespread disease outbreaks or epidemics.

q: 5. The finely divided dispersion of solid particles which are not visible to the naked eye and cannot be removed by ordinary filters are known as .............
explain: Colloidal particles are extremely small (1 to 100 millimicrons) and require chemical coagulation to be removed.

q: 6. The presence of sodium chloride in water .............
explain: Sodium salts do not contribute to hardness; in fact, sodium chloride is used in the regeneration of water softeners.

q: 7. The maximum permissible quantity of iron and manganese in water for domestic purposes should be .............
explain: Concentrations above 0.3 ppm can cause staining of laundry/fixtures and impart a metallic taste to the water.

q: 8. The maximum permissible quantity of lead in water for domestic supplies is .............
explain: Lead is a cumulative poison. Standards are extremely strict, generally limiting it to 0.05 ppm or even 0.01 ppm in modern codes.

q: 9. B-coli or E-coli are harmless organisms but their presence in water indicates the .............
explain: E-coli are 'indicator organisms'. Their presence proves fecal contamination, meaning dangerous pathogens might also be present.

q: 10. The bacteria which require oxygen for the survival is known as .............
explain: Aerobic bacteria use dissolved oxygen in water to break down organic matter.

q: 11. The area of the opening in screens should be such that the velocity of flow through them does not exceed .............
explain: Keeping velocity low prevents debris from being forced through the screen or getting wedged tightly in the openings.

q: 12. The under drainage system in a slow sand filters .............
options: receives and collects the filtered water
allows back washing for cleaning the filter
explain: Unlike rapid filters, slow sand filters are cleaned by scraping the top layer, so the under-drain system is only for collection.

q: 13. An arrangement for back washing is provided in .............
explain: Backwashing (reversing water flow to expand the sand bed) is the standard method for cleaning rapid sand filters.

q: 14. The time of contact for chlorination should be at least .............
explain: Chlorine requires a 'contact time' (usually 20-30 minutes) to successfully react with and kill microorganisms.

q: 15. The prevent formation of crystalline hydrates of 'Ice' of chlorine, the chlorine supply cylinders are kept at a temperature from .............
explain: Maintaining a moderate temperature prevents the chlorine from forming solid hydrates which could block valves and pipes.

q: 16. The apparatus used for feeding chlorine into water is called .............
explain: A chlorinator is a mechanical device designed to regulate and inject precise amounts of chlorine gas or liquid into a water stream.

q: 17. The process of removing excess chlorine from water is called .............
explain: De-chlorination is necessary when the residual chlorine level is too high for safe or pleasant consumption.

q: 18. The lime soda process of water softening .............
options: is suitable for turbid and acidic water
explain: The Lime-Soda process provides several side benefits, including disinfection (due to high pH) and assisting in coagulation.

q: 19. The minimum size of as fire hydrants is
explain: For effective fire fighting, a minimum diameter of 10 cm is generally required to ensure sufficient water discharge and pressure.

q: 20. The pipe joint commonly used in pumping stations is
explain: Flanged joints are preferred in pumping stations and treatment plants because they are easy to assemble and disassemble for maintenance.

q: 21. In primary settling tank, suspended solids are reduced from
explain: A well-designed primary sedimentation tank can remove approximately 40-70% of the suspended solids through gravity settling.

q: 22. An industry that insists on colour free water is
explain: The tanning industry requires high-quality, colour-free water to prevent staining or affecting the quality of the leather.

q: 23. Turbidity is the ability of water to
explain: Turbidity is fundamentally a measurement of light scattering caused by particles in the water.

q: 24. Due to highly turbid waters efficiency of the following operation gets affected
explain: High turbidity leads to rapid clogging of filter beds (especially rapid sand filters), requiring frequent backwashing and reducing overall efficiency.

q: 25. If 20 ml of an odours water sample is needed 180 ml of odour free distilled water produce 200 ml of odour free mixture, then the threshold odour number (TON) is
explain: TON is calculated as (Volume of Sample + Volume of Distilled Water) / Volume of Sample. Here, $(20 + 180) / 20 = 10$.

q: 26. Suspended solids are undesirable in domestic waters because they
explain: Suspended solids make water look dirty or muddy, which is primarily an aesthetic concern for the user.

q: 27. Volatile solids represent
explain: Volatile solids are those that burn off at high temperatures (550-600°C), representing the organic fraction of the solids.

q: 28. The content of total solids in drinking water shall not be greater than
explain: WHO and various national standards usually set 500 mg/L as the desirable limit for Total Dissolved Solids (TDS) in drinking water.

q: 29. pH of a water sample is 7 pH of another water sample quantity is 8, then pH of the mixture is
explain: pH is logarithmic; you must average the hydrogen ion concentrations, not the pH numbers. The result is always closer to the lower pH value.

q: 30. Higher pH for water is undesirable because
options: it corrodes zinc, copper and lead pipes
it promotes growth of iron and sulphur bacteria
explain: At high pH (>8.5), the efficiency of chlorine as a disinfectant decreases because the hypochlorous acid (HOCl) dissociates into the less effective hypochlorite ion (OCl-).

q: 31. Chloride that is insoluble in water is
explain: Silver chloride ($AgCl$) is famously insoluble and forms a white precipitate, which is the basis for the Mohr's method of chloride testing.

q: 32. A desirable feature of hardness is ...........
options: scales formed inside pipes protect them from corrosion
explain: A thin layer of calcium carbonate scale (hardness) on the inner surface of metal pipes acts as a protective coating, preventing the pipe from corroding or leaching metals like lead into the water.

q: 33. Excess concentration of sodium salts in water causes ...........
explain: Sodium contributes to the total dissolved solids (TDS) and can impact the 'Pseudo-hardness' of water, though it doesn't cause true scale-forming hardness like Ca/Mg.

q: 34. For health, presence of traces of the following elements is a must in drinking water ...........
explain: Traces of fluoride (around 1 mg/l) prevent dental caries, and iodine is essential for the proper functioning of the thyroid gland to prevent goitre.

q: 35. An indicator organism ...........
options: is of human origin but not found in water
harmless bacterium found in some types of waters
should produce more gas when incubated
explain: The key requirement for a good indicator is that it must be present whenever pathogens are present, meaning it must originate from the same source (human/animal intestines).

q: 36. A shadow well is one tapping an aquifer ...........
options: sandwiched in between two impervious layers
runs through a number of strata
explain: A shallow well (often called an unconfined or phreatic well) taps the uppermost water table which is not under pressure and is nearest to the ground surface.

q: 37. A coagulant aid is one which ...........
explain: Coagulant aids (like activated silica or polyelectrolytes) are added to produce larger, heavier, and tougher flocs, especially when the water is very cold or very low in turbidity.

q: 38. Back washing is highly effective in case of ...........
explain: Rapid sand and pressure filters are cleaned by reversing the flow of water (backwashing) to agitate the bed and remove trapped impurities. Slow sand filters are cleaned by scraping the top layer.

q: 39. A main disadvantage of chlorine as disinfectant is ...........
explain: Chlorine is a strong oxidizing agent and, in the presence of moisture, is highly corrosive to metal pipes and equipment.

q: 40. Besides disinfection chlorination is effective in the removal of ...........
explain: Chlorine oxidizes organic coloring matter and iron/manganese compounds, effectively bleaching and reducing the color of the water.

q: 41. CaCO3 gets precipitated at a pH of ............
explain: To effectively remove carbonate hardness, the pH must be raised to around 9.5 to allow Calcium Carbonate to settle out.

q: 42. Carbonate hardness is due to ............
explain: Carbonate hardness (temporary hardness) is primarily caused by the bicarbonates and carbonates of calcium and magnesium.

q: 43. A disadvantage of interlaced system is ............
explain: In an interlaced or grid system, pipes are connected in loops, which increases the total quantity and length of piping required compared to a tree system.

q: 44. Sedimentation aided by coagulation is adopted ............
options: where biological treatment is to follow next
when industrial wastes are blended with sanitary sewage
when phosphates are less in sewage
explain: Coagulation is necessary when dealing with complex industrial effluents (dyes, chemicals) that wouldn't settle under gravity alone.

q: 45. Agent responsible for ecological imbalance is ............
explain: Human activities like industrialization, deforestation, and pollution are the primary drivers of modern ecological instability.
